key_insight: This review traces how materials information extraction has evolved from rule-based pipelines to multimodal LLMs and agentic systems that support materials discovery.
engineering_relevance: Automated literature extraction can populate materials databases and knowledge graphs to support research assistance and, when integrated with autonomous laboratories, closed-loop optimization.
method: Review rule-based, NLP, transformer-encoder, and LLM extraction approaches.
Examine extraction across text, tables, and figures.
Assess generated datasets, extraction accuracy, computational costs, and pipeline design.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a critical assessment of datasets and extraction methods but provides no numerical accuracy or cost results and highlights scarce reliable benchmarks.
watch_item: Reliable sample-level linking of structure, properties, processing, and performance remains an open challenge, complicated by inconsistent terminology across document modalities.
paper_title: Automated Materials Data and Knowledge Extraction using Machine Learning and Large Language Models
